data.narrative:
Normal Computing is a Series B semiconductor chip company founded by Matthias Tan and Faris Sbahi that has raised $75.5M to date. The valuation framework draws on a comparison set of 8 private peers and 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), with relevant private comparables including Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, d-Matrix, and DEEPX across Series A through Series C stages.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $76M raised proxy, yielding $143M. Peer-median analysis across 5 same-sector comparables—spanning valuations from $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $11.0B (SambaNova, Series A)—produces a $2.0B median. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples cannot be applied due to unavailable revenue disclosure. The wide peer range ($529M–$11.0B) reflects heterogeneity in market positioning and funding trajectory within frontier semiconductor infrastructure.

Triangulation across the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $122M (floor) to $2.3B (ceiling), with a median of $1.1B. Key uncertainties include product-market maturity relative to the peer set, revenue traction not visible in public filings, and the significant valuation dispersion among Series A peers, suggesting stage-to-stage comparability carries material estimation risk.
